content.value: A recursive method calls itself on a smaller subproblem. A base case returns without another recursive call, and every valid recursive path must progress toward it. Trace the call stack: code before the recursive call runs while descending; code after it runs while unwinding. A missing or unreachable base case can exhaust the stack.
factorial(3) returns 3 * 2 * 1 * 1 = 6. Each call has its own n. Negative n would move away from zero in this implementation, and large n would overflow int even if recursion terminates.
Practice: trace the example by hand, change one input, and explain how the result changes. Check an empty or boundary case when the preconditions allow it.
